title: UI Half Marathon 2026 Review: Racing Through Indonesia's Top University Campus
seo_title: UI Half Marathon 2026 Review | Universitas Indonesia
meta_description: UI Half Marathon 2026 review: October 11 at Universitas Indonesia's Depok campus -- an alumni-organised race through one of Indonesia's top universities.
dek: Set for 11 October 2026 on the Universitas Indonesia campus in Depok, this alumni-organised race runs through the grounds of one of Indonesia's three top-ranked universities, straddling the Depok-South Jakarta border.
verdict: The UI Half Marathon is organised by ILUNI UI, the Universitas Indonesia alumni association -- giving it genuine institutional backing rather than a purely commercial promoter. UI is the oldest institution of higher education in Indonesia, ranked among the country's top three universities alongside Gadjah Mada and Bandung Institute of Technology, with a sprawling campus built specifically to accommodate the university's modernization since the mid-1980s. That gives the race a genuinely scenic, tree-lined academic setting distinct from the mall- and stadium-anchored venues dominating most of this research batch. Registration status wasn't yet announced at the time of this research.

paragraphs: The race is organised by ILUNI UI, the alumni association of Universitas Indonesia, offering 21.1K, 10K and 5K distances at the university's Depok campus. sections.heading: A Campus Built for This
paragraphs: The Depok campus, located in the northern part of the city on the border with South Jakarta, was built in the mid-1980s to accommodate the university's modernisation and now houses most of UI's faculties, including engineering, law, economics and public health. [2] Sprawling academic campuses like this typically offer wide, tree-lined internal roads well suited to a race course -- a genuinely different running environment from the malls, stadiums and city plazas hosting most other races in this research batch.

sections.heading: Institutional Rather Than Commercial Backing
paragraphs: Organisation by an alumni association rather than a commercial race promoter or corporate brand gives this event a different character from the sportswear-, beverage-, and fintech-backed races covered elsewhere in this research. [1] It's a similar model to the Malioboro Run's bank-organised structure, suggesting community and institutional investment over pure commercial branding.
